title: profiling-tooling-and-scripts-runbook-v2
content:
Purpose:
This runbook collects the canonical profiling tooling, scripts, and CI job patterns we use to investigate serving-runtime performance regressions (CPU, memory, and latency). It covers local repros, perf CI, flamegraph generation, trace collection, and common troubleshooting steps.

Scope:
- Low-level CPU/memory profiling for the runtime (C++ / CUDA / Python glue).
- End-to-end request traces and span correlation (OpenTelemetry / Jaeger).
- Perf CI job configuration and artifact storage for regression investigation.
- Lightweight sampling tools for production-safe collection.

When to use this doc:
- A CI performance alert fires (latency or token/sec regression).
- A nightly benchmark deviates >5% from baseline.
- Triaging customer-reported latency spikes.

Core components and where they live:
- Perf CI (GitHub Actions): .github/workflows/perf-ci.yml (serving-runtime repo).
- Flamegraph generation scripts: infra/perf/scripts/gen_flame.sh and gen_pyflame.sh.
- Trace collectors: otel-collector configs in infra/tracing/otel-collector.yaml.
- Artifact storage: gs://perf-artifacts/<job>/<commit>/ (CPU profiles, flamegraphs, pcap-ish traces).
- Dashboards: Grafana "serving/runtime-performance" (linked above).

Typical workflow: triage -> reproduce -> collect -> analyze -> mitigate
1) Triage
- Check perf CI job result and baseline diff. Look at token/sec, p50/p95 latencies, memory RSS.
- Confirm commit range: who changed runtime, scheduler, batching, or kernel selection.
- Check related alerts in Sentry/Jira tag (SERV-512, etc.).

2) Reproduce locally (recommended on a small instance matching test infra)
- Grab the failing commit and the previous baseline commit. Build both with identical build flags.
- Use the perf benchmark harness: ./bench/run_benchmark.sh --model llama-7b --seq 512 --batch 8 --tokens 1024 --warmup 50 --iters 200
- Ensure the same quantization/profile is used as in CI (see bench/configs/<config>.yaml).

3) Collect CPU profile (Linux perf + flamegraph)
- For C++: sudo perf record -F 99 -p <pid_of_runtime> -g -- sleep 60
- For sampling Python wrappers: use py-spy: sudo py-spy record -o profile.svg --pid <pid> --duration 60 --native
- Generate flamegraph (assuming perf.data):
  - perf script -i perf.data > out.perf
  - ./infra/perf/scripts/stackcollapse-perf.pl out.perf > out.folded
  - ./infra/perf/scripts/flamegraph.pl out.folded > flame.svg
- Common gotchas: perf needs matching kernel debug symbols for meaningful stacks. Use perf-build container used by CI when possible.

4) GPU-side hotspots
- Use nvprof/ncu for short runs on staging. Example: ncu --target-processes all -o ncu_report ./runtime_binary --args
- For CUDA kernels, capture per-kernel time and occupancy. Export to CSV and compare across commits.

5) Memory allocations and leaks
- For host allocations: heaptrack or massif (valgrind massif) for long-lived leaks. Example: valgrind --tool=massif ./runtime_binary --args
- For GPU memory: use NVIDIA DCGM and the driver-level metrics (nvml) and our agent that logs every allocation when debug mode is enabled.

6) Tracing (request-level)
- Enable OpenTelemetry spans in staging: set OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT to staging-otel-collector and OTEL_SAMPLING_PROBABILITY=0.25 for detailed runs.
- Use span attribute tags: request_id, route, model_id, batch_size, seq_len, kv_cache_hit_ratio. These are essential for correlating backend profiles to high-latency requests.
- Collect Jaeger traces: query by request_id in Jaeger UI and click links to correlating flamegraphs (stored in artifact bucket with same request_id).

7) Perf CI job patterns
- Each PR touching serving-runtime triggers perf-ci-smoke (lightweight) and perf-ci-regression (nightly).
- perf-ci-regression runs on pinned hardware images and stores artifacts to gs://perf-artifacts/<job>/<commit>/. Artifacts: perf.data, flame.svg, bench-raw.json, traces/ (OTel).
- Thresholds: token/sec drop >3% or p95 latency increase >5% mark the run as FAIL and open a perf-alert issue.
- How to reproduce a CI run locally: use infra/perf/ci_local_runner.sh --commit <sha> --job perf-ci-regression

8) Automated analysis tooling (quick checks)
- bench/compare.py --base <sha> --head <sha> --artifact-bucket gs://perf-artifacts outputs a short summary with suspicious function-level regressions (hot functions increased CPU%).
- flame-diff: infra/perf/scripts/flame_diff.py old.svg new.svg > diff.txt (high level delta by stack).

9) Runbook for an active perf regression
- Step 1: Pin failing commit and baseline commit. Notify eng-serving-runtime channel with minimal context and attach CI artifacts.
- Step 2: Run local benchmark to reproduce. If non-reproducible, run CI repro job (re-run the failing perf CI with --collect-full).
- Step 3: Collect flamegraphs for both baseline and head. Run flame-diff and bench/compare.py.
- Step 4: If diff points to a single function or file, annotate PR and bisect if necessary. If diff shows multiple areas, consider environmental drift (kernel versions, driver updates).
- Step 5: Prepare a revert or patch and validate on perf CI.

10) Production-safe sampling and collection
- For production high-QPS traffic, use 0.1% sampling by default. Increase sampling rate only during controlled investigations and coordinate with SRE.
- Use eBPF-based lightweight stacks (our infra/perf/collectors/ebpf_sampler) for low-overhead stack sampling. Command: sudo ./ebpf_sampler --duration 120 --out /tmp/ebpf.perf

11) Artifact naming conventions
- <job>/<commit>/<run_id>/perf.data
- <job>/<commit>/<run_id>/flame.svg
- <job>/<commit>/<run_id>/bench-raw.json
- <job>/<commit>/<run_id>/traces/<request_id>.json

12) Common root causes and guidance
- Hidden allocations in tokenizer/path: check python wrapper and string joins.
- KV cache copy-on-write: ensure we're not memcpy-ing cache on every request for batch size >1.
- Scheduler backpressure: long-tail batch formation due to async queueing; inspect scheduler histograms.
- Kernel selection regressed: new quantization kernels may underperform for short sequences. Run kernel microbenchmarks in infra/bench/kernels.

13) Troubleshooting checklist (quick):
- Reproducible locally? yes/no
- CI artifacts exist? link
- Flamegraphs for base/head collected? link
- GPU metrics captured? (SM utilization, mem bw)
- Any recent infra upgrades (kernel, driver, container base)?

14) Helpful scripts and commands (location in repo)
- infra/perf/scripts/gen_flame.sh --pid <pid> --out flame.svg
- infra/perf/scripts/collect_otlp.sh --duration 120 --out traces.zip
- bench/run_benchmark.sh --model <model> --seq <n> --batch <b> --iters 200
- infra/perf/ci_local_runner.sh --job perf-ci-regression --commit <sha>

15) Ownership and escalation
- Primary owner: eng-serving-runtime perf lead (Maya Patel).
- Secondary: SRE (Jordan Lee).
- If artifacts inconclusive after 48 hours, escalate to Applied ML and Runtime Leads (Alex Kim, Priya Singh).

Appendix: Example flamegraph generation script (gen_flame.sh)
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
PID=$1
OUT=${2:-flame.svg}
sudo perf record -F 99 -p $PID -g -- sleep 60
perf script -i perf.data > out.perf
# stackcollapse-perf.pl and flamegraph.pl assumed to be in PATH (Brendan Gregg tools)
stackcollapse-perf.pl out.perf > out.folded
flamegraph.pl out.folded > $OUT
echo "Flamegraph saved to $OUT"

Notes and todos:
- Add an automated collector in staging that correlates request-level traces with perf samples for the top 1% slowest requests nightly. (todo: SERV-689)
- Improve perf CI reproducibility: capture full container image and host kernel in artifacts.
- Add more kernel microbenchmarks for quantized ops.

Contact: Maya Patel (maya@redwood.ai) — ping in #eng-serving-runtime for quick help.
